root_cause.text: The nx842 crypto context code allocated multi-page bounce buffers with `__get_free_pages(order=BOUNCE_BUFFER_ORDER)` but freed them as single pages with `free_page()` in both the allocation error path and `nx842_crypto_free_ctx()`, causing improper deallocation and leaks.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `free_page((unsigned long)ctx->sbounce)` and `free_page((unsigned long)ctx->dbounce)` to `free_pages(..., BOUNCE_BUFFER_ORDER)` in `drivers/crypto/nx/nx-842.c`, and the CVE description explicitly states the buffers are allocated with `__get_free_pages()` using `BOUNCE_BUFFER_ORDER` (order 2) but released with `free_page()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the error-path cleanup to free bounce buffers with the correct page order after allocation failure.
intent_record.what: In the allocation failure path of nx842_crypto_alloc_ctx(), the cleanup calls for ctx->sbounce and ctx->dbounce were changed from free_page((unsigned long)...) to free_pages((unsigned long)..., BOUNCE_BUFFER_ORDER).
intent_record.how: This makes the deallocation match the earlier __get_free_pages() allocation size, ensuring the full multi-page bounce buffers are released correctly instead of treating them as single pages.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix bounce buffer deallocation to use the correct page order when freeing nx842 crypto context memory.
intent_record.what: In nx842_crypto_free_ctx(), the two calls that freed ctx->sbounce and ctx->dbounce were changed from free_page((unsigned long)...) to free_pages((unsigned long)..., BOUNCE_BUFFER_ORDER).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the bounce buffers are now released with the same allocation order that was used to obtain them, ensuring the full multi-page allocation is correctly freed instead of treating each buffer as a single page.

candidates.rationale: ctx->dbounce was allocated with __get_free_pages(order=BOUNCE_BUFFER_ORDER), so freeing it with free_page() incorrectly releases only a single page instead of the full multi-page allocation, causing improper deallocation/leak.
This cleanup path uses free_page() on memory allocated by __get_free_pages(order=BOUNCE_BUFFER_ORDER), which mismatches the allocator and leads to incorrect freeing and leaks.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line frees ctx->dbounce with free_page() even though the buffer was allocated with __get_free_pages(order=BOUNCE_BUFFER_ORDER), so it only releases a single page instead of the full multi-page allocation, causing improper deallocation/leak.
